body:
`AnalyticHolderExtensibleOptionEngine` searches for a zero of
`c(S) - A - S + X1` without bounding its Newton iterations. With a
negative dividend yield this function can remain positive, so the
required root need not exist.

Locate its minimum analytically and use an infinite upper critical
price when exercise never beats extension. Reject call configurations
whose extension regions the current formula cannot represent,
including those that would otherwise take the vanilla-price shortcut.
Bound all four Newton searches at 100 steps and reject invalid steps.

On Linux with GCC 13.3.0:

| Case | `84fbf0a0e` | Quadrature |
|---|---:|---:|
| No-root call, first regression row | Timed out after 20 s | 3.51340009 |
| No-root call, second regression row | Timed out after 20 s | 15.84525780 |
| Two roots below the first strike | 18.06229040 | 25.36335667 |

With this change all three match the quadrature values within the test's 1e-4 tolerance.

`testHolderExtensibleOptionNegativeDividendYield` checks supported
prices against numerical integration with mpmath 1.3.0 at an absolute
tolerance of 1e-4, and checks errors for unsupported call regions and
saturated Newton derivatives. Rejection intentionally replaces some
previously returned prices.

Checked on Ubuntu 24.04 with GCC 13.3.0, Boost 1.83.0, Release and
`QL_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON`: all four `ExtensibleOptionsTests`
cases pass in C++17 and C++20. With the production files at
`84fbf0a0e`, the new test does not finish (stopped after 300 s).

This does not address the existing negative-yield put discrepancies
or change the absolute 0.001 Newton residual tolerance.
